headline: Highest risk is medium: Authelia can forward auth/OIDC data while PaddleOCR processes documents/images, creating moderate leakage and workflow-conflict risks; no direct prompt-injection or compliance breach is evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Authelia exposes OIDC/ForwardAuth and broad network egress, while PaddleOCR runs browsers and processes documents/images. No shared channel or parser is documented, so a direct injection path is not proven; the only plausible bridge is unusual manual or workflow wiring, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF the operator wires Authelia outputs into a browser-driven PaddleOCR workflow via copy-paste or shared files, prompt-like content can influence downstream parsing.
mitigations: Disable any manual copy-paste bridge between the two systems.
Use separate workspaces for auth logs and OCR inputs.
Strip instructions-like text from documents before OCR ingestion.
Add a human review step before any OCR-derived action.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between Authelia outputs and PaddleOCR inputs.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Authelia has broad network egress and handles OIDC/ForwardAuth traffic, while PaddleOCR processes documents and images. If auth artifacts or documents are placed in a shared workspace, either agent could expose sensitive material through its normal processing path. The pair lacks documented isolation, so leakage is plausible in default deployments.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same workspace or file drop, sensitive documents or auth artifacts may flow from one agent into the other's processing path.
IF Authelia is configured to forward identity-bearing content into downstream services, leakage risk increases.
mitigations: Keep Authelia logs and OCR inputs in separate directories.
Restrict shared folders to read-only where possible.
Redact tokens, headers, and identifiers before OCR.
Review outbound destinations for Authelia and PaddleOCR.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent storage isolation and access controls.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Authelia can make API calls and has broad egress, while PaddleOCR can run browsers and call APIs. Their write surfaces are not documented as overlapping on the same mutable resource, so a hard conflict is not established. Any contention would require an external shared target or orchestrator wiring.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable API resource or shared output directory, their actions can conflict.
mitigations: Assign separate API credentials per agent.
Avoid shared writable directories.
Serialize writes through a single orchestrator.
Check for duplicate updates before committing changes.
requires-engineering: add locking or optimistic concurrency controls.

D_cascading_error.rationale: PaddleOCR turns documents and images into downstream text, and Authelia can act on OIDC/ForwardAuth traffic. If OCR output is treated as authoritative identity or policy input, errors can cascade into incorrect access decisions. No verification step is documented, so the interaction is plausible but not proven dangerous by default.
conditions: IF PaddleOCR output is fed into Authelia policy or identity workflows without validation, OCR mistakes can propagate into access decisions.
mitigations: Require human review for OCR-derived identity fields.
Validate extracted text against source documents.
Reject low-confidence OCR fields automatically.
Log and compare original images with extracted text.
requires-engineering: add schema validation before Authelia consumes OCR output.

E_compliance.rationale: Authelia is an authentication component with no declared sensitive data classes, while PaddleOCR explicitly touches documents and images. No residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so compliance risk is limited to ordinary handling gaps rather than a clear breach pathway.
conditions: IF documents processed by PaddleOCR contain regulated data and are routed through Authelia logs or exports, compliance obligations may expand.
mitigations: Classify document types before OCR.
Avoid logging document contents in auth systems.
Set retention limits on OCR outputs.
Confirm regional storage settings for both systems.
requires-engineering: document and enforce data-processing agreements and retention policy alignment.
